D004-D007_h024.question: I’ve been feeling down lately—really down—like everything’s pointless. I don’t sleep well, barely eat, and can’t remember the last time I felt good about anything. But that’s not even what’s really weighing on me. For over a year now, I’ve *known*—not thought, not feared, but *known*—that the earth’s core has stopped rotating. Scientists haven’t announced it yet because they’re hiding it, trying to avoid panic. But I can feel the changes: the days are darker, the air feels heavier, and animals act strange. In six months, gravity’s gonna fail completely. The world as we know it will end. I still go to work every day—hard to stop, when you’re a foreman and guys depend on you—but I’ve had to pull back from friends. They think I’m “stressed,” “overworked.” But I’m not crazy. I just *see* what others don’t. The sadness comes and goes—maybe a few weeks at a time—but this *truth*? That’s been with me, clear as daylight, every day for more than a year. Even when I don’t feel depressed, I still *know* what’s coming.

    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)

D004-D007_h025.question:
I’ve been having a really tough time lately, especially with my girlfriend. I know she says everything’s fine, but I can feel it—she’s been distant, canceling plans, not replying to messages for hours. I’ve checked her social media, and she’s posting photos with this guy from work, always laughing, close together. I know she’s cheating, even though she denies it. I’ve gone through her phone before—just once—and didn’t find anything concrete, but that doesn’t mean it’s not happening.

I’ll admit, I’ve been feeling down—low energy, not sleeping well, lost interest in things I used to love, like gaming or even coding side projects. Some days it’s hard to get out of bed. But honestly, most of my motivation is still there—my app update launched last week, and I’ve been keeping up with deadlines, maybe even overworking. The thing is, even when I feel depressed, the thought about her cheating is always in my head, constant, clear—day and night. There have been times, especially during work sprints, where I felt pretty stable mood-wise, but the jealousy never went away. It’s been like this for over six months. The sadness comes and goes, but the suspicion? That’s been there the whole time.
D004-D007_h025.options:
A. Delusional Disorder
    B. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    C. Binge-Eating Disorder
    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
